newsitem.title: CHINA: China to issue more corporate bonds in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China to issue more corporate bonds in 1997.

text.p: China is expected to shift the focus of debt issue next year to corporate bonds after three record years of treasury bond releases have brought outstanding state debt to its highest level, analysts said on Monday.
Beijing is telling firms to rely less on loans from state banks and to raise more money through the market, indicating a greater willingness to allow corporate bonds, they said.
The Finance Ministry has this year issued 220 billion yuan ($26.51 billion) worth of state debt, about 10 times the total value of corporate bonds issued, official figures show.
In the 1990-95 period, the total of treasury bond issues was 370 billion yuan while the total for corporate bonds was just over 60 billion yuan, the figures show.
Industry analysts estimate the corporate bond issues in 1997 will total about 50 billion yuan, while the total for issue of T-bonds and T-bills will be slightly higher than in 1996.

"After three successive record years, the current level of T-bond issue is already very high," said one T-bond trader with a major Chinese securities house. "But the state has put tight controls on the level of corporate bond issues."

The Shanghai-based Business News said in a recent report that this year's T-bond issue would amount to around three percent of China's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) this year, about the same level as for a developed country.
The newspaper said this year's issue would cover 25 percent of the state's budgetary expenditure, which it described as an excessive level.

After a peak year in 1992 when 26 billion yuan worth of corporate bonds were issued, Beijing approved the issue of only two billion yuan in 1993 and 4.5 billion yuan in 1994, partly for fear of fuelling high inflation.
"The central government has recently stressed that companies should use more market means to raise money," said Lu Weiming, a T-bill trader with China Guotai Securities.
"This year, it has allowed more companies to issue stocks to raise money and the market expects the state to allow the issue of more corporate bonds next year," he added.
"The central government is now giving the green light to more companies to issue bonds," said a Chinese banker. "More approvals have recently been given in key sectors."
Seven units of China National Petrochemical Corp have been given approval to issue 1.34 billion yuan in corporate bonds in early December, the China Securities newspaper said on Saturday.
The mother company will provide a guarantee for the bonds, which will have a three-year term and annual interest of 10.5 percent, to be paid once on maturity, it said.
Earlier, the Ministry of Railways was given approval to issue 3.5 billion yuan worth of bonds in the near future to help finance expansion of the country's rail system.

Companies under China's Ministry of Power Industry plan to make a public offering of 1.0752 billion yuan worth of bonds to domestic investors shortly to fund expansion of output of electricity, official newspapers have reported.
Corporate bond issues in China are approved by the State Planning Commission and the People's Bank of China, the central bank. Officials declined to comment.
